estimates.source: Engine display values transcribed verbatim from the run record's display block and the method comparison table; nothing here was recomputed.
estimates.primary: Inverse-variance-weighted odds ratio 1.56 (95% CI 1.39-1.75), p=4.0x10^-14, 79 instruments.

instrumentStrength.reading: No instrument falls below the conventional mean-F>10 relevance heuristic, the minimum being 29.9 and the median 40.6. That number tests relevance and nothing else. It says nothing about independence or the exclusion restriction.

harmonisation.reading: All 79 supplied instruments were retained. Four palindromic variants resolved without being dropped, and none was lost for absence of outcome data.

heterogeneity.reading: Q is significant under both the MR-Egger model and the inverse-variance-weighted model. A fixed-effect reading is not supported, and at this instrument count the between-instrument spread is real.

pleiotropy.reading: The MR-Egger intercept is indistinguishable from zero (p=0.67). Under the InSIDE assumption that is a check for directional pleiotropy, not evidence that pleiotropy is absent, and at this configuration its power is low.

presso.reading: The global test sits below the display floor and 2 outlier variants were corrected. The corrected estimate falls inside the primary interval and the distortion test shows no change. The outlier resolution equals the 0.0500 threshold exactly, which points to an unstable outlier set and not to a clean correction.

radialAndConmix.reading: Both secondary diagnostics point beyond the primary model to further heterogeneity: a radial global test well below the display floor with 10 outlier variants, and a contamination estimate near one half whose interval excludes zero.

assumptionStatus.reading: Direction cannot be tested, because no instrument row carries both sample sizes, which leaves the Steiger check unavailable instead of negative. Whether the exposure and outcome samples overlap is undetermined, so the direction of any overlap bias is unestablished too. Scale metadata for both sides is unknown: the exposure effect is expressed per the supplied SD unit and the outcome on the log-odds scale, and nothing in the supplied columns allowed a unit check.

limitationsVisibleInOutput: This job directory has no queue record, so terminal state rests on the job's own result file instead of an independent queue entry.
No live status query was possible this session.
The instruments are a historical pre-clumped cache export. The original clumping parameters were never serialized, and LD independence was not rechecked.
Steiger directionality cannot be computed from the supplied columns, which leaves causal direction resting on the design and not on a computed test.
Whether the two GWAS sources overlap is undetermined, and the direction of any overlap bias is unestablished.
The outcome associations belong to the BMI variant set and not to an independently selected coronary heart disease instrument set. The analysis runs forward only.
Instrument strength is a relevance check and does not validate the exclusion restriction. The funnel-style asymmetry diagnostics carry assumptions of their own.
On effect scale: the exposure effect is per one SD of the supplied unit and the outcome is on the log-odds scale, and neither could be verified from the supplied columns.
